reason: C2 is an AC/compensation (Miller-like) capacitor between the output and internal node net017; removing it usually keeps the DC amplification path intact. Caveat: it may reduce stability/phase margin and increase ringing or peaking in transient/AC response.

C1 is a shunt capacitor at net017 that mainly filters/high-frequency shapes that node; deleting it typically preserves the basic DC operating point and gain behavior. Caveat: net017 becomes noisier/faster, which can change bandwidth and potentially worsen stability depending on C2’s role.

M10 is a diode-connected PMOS likely used as a bias/helper load for node net015; the core amplification to VOUT1 can still be provided by M11 with M1/M3. Caveat: removing M10 can shift the bias point at net015 and change gain/output swing because it may be setting current/voltage for the PMOS load network.
impact_estimate: Low-to-medium (bias point and gain may shift)
